I will still follow the wheat-maize rotation on all 10.1 mu, because that is what fits our land and water, and I know how to manage it steadily. I do not start from zero every year. I look at what I did last year, what neighbors around Quzhou are doing, and then I adjust a little. With well irrigation, I am not as afraid of drought as dryland people, so I will keep fertilizer and water fairly solid. I would rather spend a bit more on fertilizer than lose yield, because once yield drops, that money does not come back. For wheat, I will use an improved variety, put enough base fertilizer, and give the main water at overwintering, jointing, and grain filling if needed. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, because around here hybrids usually give better ears and more stable yield. I will not cut fertilizer too hard on maize, because after wheat harvest the season is tight and maize has to grow fast. On 10.1 mu, I still calculate input costs, but this is not such a tiny area that I must save on every bag. Labor in the family is limited since some people work off-farm, so I will keep the management simple and dependable: rotary tillage, a few key irrigations, and pesticide only when the field really needs it.
